correctness.rationale: The proof starts with the complete Matrix–Tree cofactor for two marked vertices having nested but unequal allowed-neighbor sets; the Schur complement and rank-two determinant give F_n(a,b) exactly. Three disjoint categories of ordered marked pairs recover the two-time second moment. An explicit first-order expansion of the ratios of mixed probabilities to one-point products yields the positive rank-two continuum kernel. Complete Prüfer-code enumeration at n=4..7 verifies the exact moment identity for every admissible pair, and an extracted standalone Python checker passes 79,130 tests. Finite computation does not substitute for the analytic proof or imply a Gaussian process limit.

value.rationale: The covariance across distinct reveal times measures persistence and turnover of isolated components, a natural local connectivity statistic not identified by single-time component-size counts or by global edge-process fluctuations. The exact finite formula, explicit strictly positive two-time scaling kernel, and its rank-two semiseparable representation give a reusable benchmark for stochastic-process limits and inference on partially uncovered trees. It requires a nontrivial asymmetric two-marked Matrix–Tree determinant rather than a substitution in the known one-time component formula.
